title: Identity Lab™: Identity as a Verb v3.0
description: Identity is not a noun. It is a verb. Trace inherited and chosen beliefs, write an identity equation, and document one seven-day act of becoming.

### INVESTIGATION 1: THE HOOK

MISSION: Meet someone who discovered who she really was.

YOU WILL PRODUCE:

● ☐ A prediction about Myah's choice

TIME: 5 minutes

DIFFICULTY:           Observe

### 📖 Read

Episode 1: The Girl Who Wrote Her Name

Meet Myah.

Myah is fifteen. She is quiet. She notices things. At the taxi rank, she watches people. She sees her mother counting coins every morning. She sees the vendors, the queue marshals, the money flowing between everyone. She writes in a small notebook.

She has never said what she notices out loud. She has never told anyone what she really thinks. She has never named who she is becoming.

One day, her teacher asks:

"Who are you?"

Myah thinks. She could say her name. Her age. Where she lives. Her family. But that is not who she is. That is just what people see.

She writes in her notebook:

"I am someone who notices. I am someone who asks questions. I am someone who wants to understand money—where it comes from, where it goes, how it works. I am someone who wants to help my mother instead of just taking from her."

She has not said this out loud. But she has written it. And writing it made it real.

She is becoming someone. She just did not have the words until she wrote them down.

But she still has not said it out loud. She still has not shown anyone. She still does not know if she believes it.

She is fifteen. She has written who she is becoming. But she has not become her yet.

### INVESTIGATION 3: THE REVELATION

MISSION: Discover the hidden truth about identity.

YOU WILL PRODUCE:
● ☐ Understanding of identity as becoming
● ☐ Prediction calibration check

TIME: 3 minutes

DIFFICULTY:           Analyse

### 📖 Read

Episode 2: What Myah Didn't Say

Myah wrote who she was becoming. She did not say it out loud. She did not show anyone. She just wrote it.

But here is what nobody told her: identity is not a noun. It is a verb.

Most people think identity is something you have. Something fixed. Something you are born with or discover once and keep forever.

But identity is not fixed. It is becoming. Every choice, every habit, every belief is a vote for the person you are becoming.

Myah wrote down who she was becoming. She did not wait to find herself. She started building herself.

But she still has not said it out loud. She still has not shown anyone. She still does not know if she believes it.

The next day, she walks past the spaza shop. She sees Sipho and Lethabo talking. Sipho is holding a packet of screws. Lethabo is showing him something—a clock.

She stops. She watches.

Sipho looks up. "You're the girl with the notebook," he says.

She nods.

"What do you write in there?" Lethabo asks.

She does not know what to say. She looks at them. She thinks about her notebook. She thinks about what she wrote.

"I write about who I'm becoming," she says.

She did not plan to say it. She just said it.

Sipho and Lethabo look at her. They do not laugh. They nod.

"Me too," Sipho says.

"Same," Lethabo says.

She walks home. She does not know what just happened. But she said it out loud.

She is fifteen. She has written who she is becoming. She has said it out loud. She still does not know if she believes it.

But she said it.

And something shifted.
